title: Digital Hammering Inspection for Social Infrastructure
content: Although conventional hammering inspection remains a standard practice across various industries, its effectiveness is often limited by a heavy reliance on the inspector’s subjective skill, leading to qualitative and inconsistent results. To address these limitations, this study introduces a digital hammering inspection system integrated with Acoustic Emission (AE) sensors, designed for enhanced quality control and long-term aging management. The system has been extensively implemented in the diagnostic evaluation of social infrastructure, encompassing both metallic and concrete structures. By leveraging the principles of natural vibration, the system provides an objective, quantitative, and recordable screening process that significantly reduces human error and ensures high-speed data acquisition. Furthermore, its lightweight design and portability facilitate seamless field application, enabling comprehensive, on-site diagnostics that are both reliable and scalable for diverse engineering environments.
